summary: A nominal fence can create false assurance: broad credentials, stale trust classifications, approval fatigue, and sensitive logs can leave the underlying risk unchanged or introduce new risk.

points.text: If the execution gateway ultimately holds a broad cloud or database credential, fine-grained model-side labels do not prevent confused-deputy actions or lateral movement.
Trust earned on one model snapshot or read-only tool set can be wrongly carried into a new provider, prompt, plugin, or write-capable environment.
Sending every uncertain action to a human produces approval fatigue; reviewers learn to approve opaque requests, shifting liability without improving control.

Full prompts, tool arguments, and outputs can contain credentials, personal data, or proprietary code. Centralizing them in an audit store expands the breach surface unless fields are minimized, redacted, and access-controlled.
